chunks: There is no adhan or iqama upon a woman, nor Jumu'ah, nor congregational prayer.

When a woman stands in her salat, she gathers her feet together and does not separate them, and she places her hands on her chest at the place of her breasts. When she performs ruku', she places her hands above her knees on her thighs so that she does not bend too much and her buttocks rise. When she intends sajdah, she sits and then prostrates, pressing herself close to the ground, and places her forearms on the ground. When she wishes to rise to standing, she lifts her head from sajdah and sits upon her buttocks, not as a man sits, then rises to standing without lifting her buttocks, moving gently upward. When she sits for the tashahhud, she raises her legs and keeps her thighs together. A free woman does not perform salat except with a head covering, while a bondwoman performs salat without a head covering.

key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: the second call announcing the start of the prayer
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the testimony recited while seated in prayer

ai.seo_question: What does Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih say about a woman's manner of performing salat?
ai.summary: This hadith presents legal rulings and etiquettes related to a woman's salat, including matters not obligatory upon her and the manner of her bodily posture in different parts of the prayer. It also states a ruling regarding head covering in salat for a free woman and a bondwoman.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: There is no call to prayer (adhan) or iqama for a woman, nor is there a Jumu’ah prayer (Jumu'ah) or congregational prayer (Jama'ah) for her.

When a woman stands in prayer, She gathers her feet together and does not spread them apart, placing her hands on her chest at the location of her breasts.
When She bows, She places her hands on her knees, on her thighs, so as not to bend too much and cause her back to rise.
When She goes to prostrate, She sits first and then prostrates, pressing her face to the ground and placing her arms on the ground.
When She rises to stand, She lifts her head from the prostration and sits on her buttocks, not in the way a man would sit. Then, She rises to stand without raising her back and hips, moving smoothly.
When She sits for the tashahhud (testification), She raises her legs and brings her thighs together. A free woman (Hura) does not pray except with a veil (niqab), while a slave woman (ama) prays without a veil.
